# Configuration

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from the config and tool group models. Do not edit by hand. -->

dev-link reads its settings from these layers. A later layer overrides an earlier one:

1. Built-in defaults (listed below).
2. The user file `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev-link/config.yaml` (usually `~/.config/dev-link/config.yaml`), if it exists.
3. The file passed with `--config FILE`. It must exist.
4. Environment variables named `DEV_LINK_*`.
5. Command-line flags.

Sections such as `server` merge key by key, so a layer only changes the keys it sets. Any other
value, including a list or the `sandbox.env` mapping, is replaced whole. The repeatable flags
`--enable`, `--disable` and `--allowed-host` are the exception: they add to the list built by the
layers below.

Unknown keys and values of the wrong type stop the server with an error that names the key and
the layer it came from. Editors that support JSON Schema can check a config file against
[config.schema.json](config.schema.json). The tools of each group and their parameters are listed
in [tools.md](tools.md).

## Environment variables

A key in a section is set with `DEV_LINK_<SECTION>__<KEY>` (two underscores), for example
`DEV_LINK_SANDBOX__NETWORK=false` or `DEV_LINK_SERVER__PORT=9000`. The top-level keys are
`DEV_LINK_STATE_DIR` and `DEV_LINK_LOG_LEVEL`. Strings and paths are used as written; other values
are read as YAML, so `false`, `30` and `[http, browser]` work.

A tool group setting is set with `DEV_LINK_GROUPS__<GROUP>__<KEY>`, for example
`DEV_LINK_GROUPS__BROWSER__HEADLESS=false`. These values are always read as YAML, so quote a string
that looks like a number or a boolean.

The workspace cannot be set from the environment. Commands run by the agent see
`DEV_LINK_WORKSPACE`, and dev-link ignores it. Other unknown `DEV_LINK_*` variables are ignored
with a warning.

## Files inside the workspace are never read

The agent can write anywhere in the workspace, so a config file there could turn off the sandbox
for the next start. dev-link never looks for config files in the workspace, and it refuses a
`--config` file or user file whose path is inside it.

## Example

```yaml
server:
  port: 9000
sandbox:
  network: false
  env:
    PORT: "3000"
tools:
  enabled: [docker]
  disabled_tools: [browser_eval]
groups:
  browser:
    headless: false
```

## Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace` | path | required | Folder exposed to the agent and the only place it can write. Usually given as the command-line argument. Must not be `/`, your home folder, or a parent of it. |
| `state_dir` | path or null | `null` | Where logs, the audit store and the sandbox home live. Must be outside the workspace. Default: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/dev-link-mcp/<folder name>-<hash>`. |
| `log_level` | one of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR` | `"INFO"` | Server log level. Lower case is accepted. |
| `groups` | mapping of string to mapping | `{}` | Settings of each tool group, keyed by group name. Each group checks its own keys at start; see Tool groups below. |

## `server`

Network address and authentication.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.host` | string | `"127.0.0.1"` | Address to bind. Auth `none` is only allowed on a loopback address. |
| `server.port` | integer (1 to 65535) | `8765` | TCP port to listen on. |
| `server.auth` | one of `path-token`, `bearer`, `none` | `"path-token"` | How MCP clients prove access. `path-token` puts a secret token in the URL path, `bearer` expects an `Authorization: Bearer` header, `none` turns auth off (loopback only). |
| `server.token` | string | `""` | Fixed token for `path-token` and `bearer` auth. Empty means a new random token on every start. At least 16 characters, using only letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `~`. |
| `server.public_url` | string | `""` | Public base URL when the server sits behind a tunnel or proxy (e.g. `https://x.trycloudflare.com`). Its hostname is accepted automatically and the banner prints public URLs. Not allowed with auth `none`. |
| `server.allowed_hosts` | list of strings | `[]` | Extra Host header values to accept, e.g. a tunnel hostname. Exact match, or `host:*` for any port. Not allowed with auth `none`. |

## `sandbox`

Isolation of agent commands.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox.backend` | one of `auto`, `bubblewrap`, `none` | `"auto"` | How agent commands are isolated. `bubblewrap` confines them to the workspace (Linux only); `none` runs them with full access to your machine, like a coding agent run directly. `auto` uses bubblewrap and refuses to start when it cannot run here (not Linux, `bwrap` missing, or user namespaces blocked); it never falls back to `none`. |
| `sandbox.network` | boolean | `true` | Allow network access inside the sandbox. |
| `sandbox.ro_paths` | list of strings | `["~/.nvm", "~/.local/bin", "~/.local/share/uv/python", "~/.sdkman", "~/.cargo/bin", "~/.rustup", "~/go", "~/.pyenv", "~/.bun", "~/.deno"]` | Host paths mounted read-only inside the sandbox in addition to the system folders. Missing paths are skipped, so one config works across machines. |
| `sandbox.rw_paths` | list of strings | `[]` | Host paths mounted read-write. Anything here is reachable by the agent. |
| `sandbox.env_passthrough` | list of strings | `["LANG", "LC_ALL", "TZ", "JAVA_HOME", "MAVEN_HOME", "GOPATH", "NVM_DIR"]` | Host environment variables copied into the sandbox. Everything else is dropped so server secrets do not leak into agent commands. |
| `sandbox.env` | mapping of string to string | `{}` | Extra environment variables for agent commands. Values must be strings: quote numbers in YAML. |

## `limits`

Timeouts, size limits and resource caps for tools.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limits.default_timeout_s` | number | `120.0` | Command timeout in seconds when the agent does not set one. |
| `limits.max_timeout_s` | number | `3600.0` | Longest timeout in seconds the agent may ask for. |
| `limits.max_output_bytes` | integer | `200000` | Bytes of command output returned to the agent; the middle is cut out beyond this. |
| `limits.max_read_bytes` | integer | `2000000` | Largest file or HTTP body, in bytes, that read tools return. |
| `limits.max_processes` | integer | `32` | Most background processes that may run at the same time. |
| `limits.memory_mb` | integer or null | `null` | Memory cap in MiB for each command and background process. Swap is not allowed, so past the cap the kernel kills the command. Enforced with a systemd user scope (`systemd-run --user`); the server refuses to start if that does not work. `null` means no cap. |
| `limits.max_pids` | integer or null | `null` | Most processes and threads each command may have at once, counting the two that bubblewrap itself uses; further forks fail. JVM and Node runtimes start many threads, so leave room. Enforced like `memory_mb`. `null` means no cap. |

## `audit`

What the audit log keeps.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.result_bytes` | integer | `256000` | Bytes of each tool call's arguments and result kept in the audit log. Longer arguments are stored as a clipped string instead of a JSON object. |
| `audit.retention_days` | integer or null | `30` | Audit events and background process logs older than this many days are deleted when the server starts. `null` keeps everything. |

## `tools`

Which tool groups are registered.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tools.enabled` | list of strings | `[]` | Groups to turn on that are off by default: the opt-in group `docker` and installed plugins. |
| `tools.disabled` | list of strings | `[]` | Tool groups to turn off, e.g. `http` or `browser`. |
| `tools.disabled_tools` | list of strings | `[]` | Single tools to remove, e.g. `run_command`. Names of tools in a group that is turned off or not installed are ignored, so one list works across machines. |

## Tool groups

Tools come in groups. Every built-in group is on unless `tools.disabled` lists it, except
`docker`, which also needs `tools.enabled` (or `--enable docker`). `tools.disabled_tools` removes
single tools. An unknown name in `tools.enabled`, `tools.disabled`, `tools.disabled_tools` or
`groups` stops the server, so a typo cannot go unnoticed.

The `browser` and `code` groups need extra packages: install `dev-link-mcp[browser]`,
`dev-link-mcp[code]`, or `dev-link-mcp[all]` for both. Without them the group is reported as not
installed, in the log, on the dashboard and by `workspace_info`, and the server starts without it.

Each group reads its settings from `groups.<name>`, merged key by key like a section. Settings
of a group that is turned off or not installed are not checked.

### Plugins

Other packages can add tool groups; see [extending.md](extending.md). An installed plugin is
loaded only when `tools.enabled` lists its name, so installing a package never adds tools by
itself. Plugins run inside the dev-link server process, outside the sandbox: install only
plugins you trust.

### `groups.system`

Workspace and server information.

No settings.

### `groups.files`

Reading, writing, editing and organising files inside the workspace.

No settings.

### `groups.search`

Content and file-name search with ripgrep, plus search-and-replace across files.

No settings.

### `groups.shell`

One-shot shell commands and code snippets, run inside the sandbox.

No settings.

### `groups.processes`

Background processes: dev servers, watchers, REPLs and other long-running commands.

No settings.

### `groups.code`

Code intelligence: outlines, symbol definitions, references and line statistics. Needs `dev-link-mcp[code]`.

No settings.

### `groups.project`

Project detection and the standard install/test/lint/format/build commands.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groups.project.long_timeout_s` | number | `600.0` | Timeout in seconds for install_deps, run_tests and run_build when the agent does not set one. `limits.max_timeout_s` still caps it. |

### `groups.http`

HTTP client tools: raw requests, readable page fetches, and downloads into the workspace.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groups.http.default_timeout_s` | number | `30.0` | Total timeout in seconds for http_request, fetch_url and download_file when the agent does not set one. Must not exceed `limits.max_timeout_s`. |
| `groups.http.download_max_bytes` | integer | `100000000` | Largest download_file result in bytes when the agent does not set one. |
| `groups.http.max_redirects` | integer | `10` | Most redirects a request follows before it fails. |

### `groups.data`

SQLite, JSON and CSV inspection tools.

No settings.

### `groups.checkpoints`

Workspace snapshots in a shadow git repository the agent cannot see.

No settings.

### `groups.tasks`

Persistent task list and notes for long agent jobs.

No settings.

### `groups.docker`

Docker containers, images and compose projects through the host docker CLI. Opt-in: off unless `tools.enabled` lists it.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groups.docker.build_timeout_s` | number | `600.0` | Timeout in seconds for docker_build, docker_compose and a detached docker_run (which may pull an image) when the agent does not set one. `limits.max_timeout_s` still caps it. |

### `groups.browser`

Headless Chromium driven through Playwright for frontend work. Needs `dev-link-mcp[browser]`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groups.browser.headless` | boolean | `true` | Run Chromium without a window. Set to false to watch the agent work on a desktop. |
| `groups.browser.max_pages` | integer | `10` | Most pages, popups included, that may be open at once. |
| `groups.browser.default_timeout_s` | number | `15.0` | Seconds a browser action waits (for an element, a load, a script) when the agent does not set a timeout. `limits.max_timeout_s` still caps it. |
| `groups.browser.idle_timeout_s` | number | `300.0` | Seconds without any browser tool call after which all pages, Chromium and the Playwright driver are closed to free their memory. The next browser call starts them again; pages open at the time must be opened again. 0 keeps them running until the server stops. |
